newsitem.title: UK: European shares smash records in early surge.
newsitem.headline: European shares smash records in early surge.

text.p: European shares rewrote the record books in the first minutes of business on Tuesday after the Wall Street bull thundered to yet another record close overnight -- its 14th this year.
"It looks like the big boys are back buying the big stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co in the United States.
The 30-share Dow jumped 78.50 points to 7,079.39 on Monday after adding 56 points on Friday following a government report of solid job growth in February with little sign of wage-driven inflation.
The Dow close eclipsed the previous record of 7,067.46 set on February 18 although most other major market gauges remained well off record levels. The Dow set 44 records for all of 1996.

News of a surge of cash into mutual funds helped stocks, analysts said. Americans put $1.49 billion into mutual funds for the three days ended on Thursday, according to Mutual Fund Trim Tab, which tracks the industry.

By mid morning, Europe's three key bourses were all at new trading records, with London's FTSE index, Europe's biggest market up 0.5 percent while France's CAC-40 index was up 0.7 percent and Germany's DAX by more than 0.8 percent.
In London, traders said shares were supported by renewed optimism over the near-term domestic interest rate outlook as well as Wall Street's impressive performance.
The FTSE 100 index was up 23.5 points at 4,460.9, passing the previous all-time high of 4,440.8 set on Monday.

"We've got another 60 points to contend with, though we would have liked to have seen more follow-through on the bond market, and a broader advance other than the Dow, as the other indices didn't make quite such good running," said one trader in London.

Traders noted renewed confidence that interest rates will not rise soon following comments from Bank of England governor Eddie George on Monday and the market took comfort from the latest weak sales data from the British Retail Consortium.
Traders said the recent batch of major British company results was on the whole encouraging, but some were still cautious of the market's seemingly unstoppable rise.

French shares steamed higher at the open, picking up a strong tailwind from another surge on Wall Street overnight. Traders said funds were staying in Paris equities, attracted by successive rises on the CAC-40 index, which was up 18.82 points at 2,728.03.
Germany's DAX index was up 29.84 points at 3,465.91 points by midmorning, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98 and eyeing its next key resistance level at 3,500.

"We will see 3,500, and maybe today," said a Frankfurt dealer, who added that he was taken aback by the pace of the market's advance, despite continued solid earnings signals for German firms from the strong dollar.
"There is nothing around to break this momentum," said another dealer. "There is no sign here of a consolidation."

In currencies, the dollar found strong bids below 1.70 marks in early trading as U.S. asset market buoyancy and receding fears about the start date for European monetary union provided solid support, analysts said.
Support for the mark in Europe eroded further as senior Bundesbank members late on Monday all said the single currency should be launched on time.
"We're seeing some good support for the dollar now," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.
The dollar had firmed to 1.7061 marks by midmorning.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria allowed for small deviations from the 3.0 percent deficit/output ratio and EMU could take place as planned in 1999 without softening the wording of the Treaty.

Bundesbank member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher and president of the European Monetary Institute Alexandre Lamfalussy also stressed that small deviations from Maastricht's "reference values" were allowed if the leeway is used sparingly.

Elsewhere, the dollar/yen was a touch softer after news of a robust 11.8 percent rise in Japanese machinery orders in January and as the benchmark three-month certificate of deposit (CD) rate rose to 0.55 percent, the highest since last August.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7061 marks and 121.78 yen compared with 1.7027 marks and 121.74 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 23.5 points at 4,460.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 18.82 points at 2,728.03.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 29.84 points at 3,465.91 points.
PRECIOUS METALS 1030 GMT
Gold fixed at $352.60 an ounce after closing at $350.75 in London on Monday.
